_comentario: First Numbers, Part 2 (winter, days 66-130): the English text of each day of Aprendo los números (content/q2.json) -- 'frase', with the day's number in words, and the text of its activity ('prompt', 'checklist', 'texto'). See content/english/q1.json and notes/02-english.md.

dias.frase: Winter begins, and eleven snowflakes fall past the window.
Grandma sews eleven buttons on Lucía's new coat.
Toby sleeps by the fire, and Dad brings in twelve logs.
This week, Lucía has read Dani twelve stories.
On Saturday, there are twelve snowmen in the park.
checklist: I know what 11 and 12 look like.
I know that 12 is 10 and 2.
I can count to 12.

dias.frase: Today is Dad's birthday, and Mum puts thirteen strawberries on the cake.
Dani hides thirteen balloons under the table.
Surprise! Fourteen friends are waiting for Dad in party hats.
Dani's present is a drawing with fourteen hearts.
That night, Lucía counts Dad's presents: fourteen!
checklist: I know what 13 and 14 look like.
I know that 14 is 10 and 4.
I can count to 14.

dias.frase: There will be fifteen butterflies in the parade, and one of them will be Lucía.
Grandma Rosa sews Lucía's wings on with fifteen buttons.
There are sixteen children in Lucía's class, and each of them will get a lollipop.
Dani is dressed as a green dragon, and Toby wears a neckerchief with sixteen stars on it.
In the parade, everyone sings and dances to sixteen songs.
checklist: I know what 15 and 16 look like.
I know that 16 is 10 and 6.
I can count to 16.

dias.frase: Marta shows the class how to make paper doves, and they make seventeen.
There are seventeen coloured pencils to paint the doves.
Marta makes one more dove, and now there are eighteen.
Together, they paint eighteen hearts for peace.
That night, from the window, Lucía counts seventeen stars.
checklist: I know what 17 and 18 look like.
I know that 18 is 10 and 8.
I can count to 18.
dias.prompt: Draw a dove of peace, in your favourite colours.

dias.frase: Lucía has a temperature, and she looks at the nineteen stars on her ceiling.
Grandma brings Lucía nineteen tangerines from the village.
So as not to get bored in bed, Lucía colours in twenty flowers.
Dani lends Lucía all his soft toys: twenty teddy bears!
On Saturday, Lucía is better, and she runs twenty laps of the park with Toby.
checklist: I know what 19 and 20 look like.
I know that 20 is 10 and 10.
I can count to 20.
dias.prompt: Draw Lucía in the park with Toby, all better.

dias.frase: On Sunday, Grandma Rosa brings twelve balls of coloured wool.
Lucía picks two balls of wool to knit with: a blue one and a red one.
Dani would rather play with Grandma's buttons, and he keeps five.
Grandma teaches Lucía to embroider fifteen stars.
By the end of the day, Lucía has knitted one small scarf, and she loves it.
checklist: I can see which group has more.
I can see which group has fewer.
I can see which groups have the same number.
dias.prompt: Draw Lucía's scarf, with coloured stripes.

dias.frase: Lucía goes to the library every Saturday, and today she takes back seven books.
The librarian keeps a book with nine cats in it for her.
Lucía looks for a book for Dani on shelf sixteen.
The book for Dani has thirteen dogs in it, and one looks like Toby.
That night, Lucía reads the book to Dani, and Dani falls asleep on page ten.
checklist: I know which number comes before.
I know which number comes after.
I can count backwards from 10.
dias.prompt: Draw the local library, with lots of books.

dias.frase: Today it is one year since Toby came to live with Lucía's family.
Lucía makes five cardboard crowns, one for each of them, Toby included.
Dani gives him his red ball, and now Toby has seven balls.
Toby gets twelve bones as presents, and he hides them under the sofa.
That night, Toby falls asleep with his seven balls.
checklist: I can read the numbers on the number line.
I know which number is missing on the line.
I can count to 20.

dias.frase: The wind is blowing really hard, and nine leaves fly down the street.
Lucía's new woolly hat nearly blows away, but she grabs it with one hand.
It is so windy that six kites are flying in the park.
The wind pushes eleven clouds across the sky, very fast.
At night, the wind dies down, and three stars come out.
checklist: I know which number is bigger.
I can put numbers in order, from smallest to biggest.
I can put them in order the other way round too.
dias.prompt: Draw a very windy day, with kites and leaves flying.

dias.frase: Marta gives each child a flowerpot, and each of them plants three seeds.
There are four flowerpots in the sun on the classroom windowsill.
A few days later, five shoots come up in Lucía's pot.
Grandma gives Dani five sunflower seeds to plant.
Now Lucía and Dani have two flowerpots on their windowsill.
checklist: I can put two groups together.
I can count how many there are altogether.
I know that 3 and 2 make 5.
dias.prompt: Draw your flowerpot, with the plant you would like to grow in it.

dias.frase: Lucía has six dinosaurs, and her favourite is the green one.
Lucía gets very cross, and eight tears roll down Dani's face.
Mum tells them that the important thing is to say sorry, and gives them seven kisses.
Together, they stick the leg back on with ten drops of glue.
By bedtime, the two of them have made friends again.
checklist: I can put two groups together, up to 10.
I know that 7 and 3 make 10.
I can say sorry when I break something.
dias.prompt: Draw Lucía and Dani mending the dinosaur.

dias.frase: In the park there are nine almond trees covered in white flowers.
Dani picks up eight fallen flowers and gives them to Lucía.
Ten swallows are flying high up in the sky.
On the way home, they see twenty butterflies among the flowers.
Lucía and Dani plant three flowers on the balcony.
checklist: I can put two groups together.
I can count on from 10.
I know the numbers up to 20.
dias.prompt: Draw the park in spring, with flowers and butterflies.

dias.frase: On Sunday, the family goes to the big park, and they see fourteen ducks on the lake.
Lucía remembers the four nicest things about the winter.
Dani is very proud: he can read six words all by himself.
Toby runs happily among the trees, and sniffs seventeen new flowers.
Lucía thinks this winter deserves twenty stars.
checklist: I know the numbers from 0 to 20.
I can compare, put in order and put together.
I know which number comes before, and which comes after.
dias.prompt: Draw what you liked best about the winter.
